title: "Help"

## How the modules work

Each module combines concise teaching sections, diagrams, clinical reasoning, and knowledge checks. Many modules use case-based learning, guiding learners through realistic patient scenarios and asking them to apply the concepts as they go.

The goal is to connect foundational knowledge with clinical decision-making: recognizing important patterns, identifying red flags, interpreting investigations in context, and considering appropriate management options.

### Learning callouts

Throughout the modules, callouts highlight different types of learning points.

::: {.callout-tip title="Pause and think"}

A short question to help you check your understanding before reading the answer.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Key idea"}

The main takeaway from a section.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="Clinical relevance"}

Why the concept matters for patient assessment, imaging, procedures, or management.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Word of caution"}

A common mistake, limitation, or point that should not be overinterpreted.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Red flag"}

An urgent clinical feature that should prompt timely assessment or escalation.
:::
